thumbnail_brief: One huge black Cape buffalo bull fills the frame, head low, the fused horn boss front and centre, mud caked on its flanks, staring straight out, while tiny Doug in his red cap crouches in the reeds in the foreground with a camera, looking the wrong way, with the words BLACK DEATH, so the title gives the paradox (a grass-eater that kills lions) and the thumbnail gives the nickname and the stare; no wounds, blood, goring or injured lions, and no BUFFALO, LION, GRASS or KG on the image. Variant B: the old bull glaring up out of a mud wallow as Doug creeps to its edge with his camera, HE'S RETIRED. Variant C: a wall of buffalo heads under a dust cloud at a shrinking waterhole, Doug in a lion-pride intern badge beside a lion already turning to run, 1,000+.
description:
Hunters call the Cape buffalo the Black Death, yet it only eats grass. Doug follows one African buffalo, then a whole herd, then a dry-season megaherd of a thousand or more, from the retired dagga boy in his mud wallow to the herd that turns around and chases the lions.

Where should we send Doug next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe and watch Doug's death counter keep climbing.
